TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the FY2027―FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: To purpose of this action is to seek Board of Trustees approval for the submission of the University of Rhode Island FY2027―FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to the State of Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: Every year it is the responsibility of the University to submit a CIP to the State of Rhode Island.
The CIP identifies and lists in order of priority capital projects (both proposed or in progress) of $1 million or more funded with unrestricted funds.
This submission is a critical and required step to secure funding to support the physical assets at the University advancing both educational and research programs.

The enclosed presentation provides updat es to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including the Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 projects, the Fine Arts Center, the Athletics Complex Renewal, the Biomedical Sciences Building, and New Undergraduate Housing.
It also provides information for the Memorial Union and Health and Counseling Center projects, which have been on hold for the last several years to prioritize housing.
The presentation also highlights several additions made to the CIP last year, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings.
These additions incl ude improving campus accessibility, access control, building envelope integrity, and refurbishment of the Carothers Library HVAC systems and the university’s water tower.

Two new projects are proposed to be added to the CIP this year, replacement of the Allen Harbor Bulkhead and Dock, which is necessary to protect the site and maintain access to our small boats that provide both educational and research support, and a project currently underway to renovate Washburn Hall and the Carlotti Building to provide space needed to empty Tucker House and Adams House in anticipation of future mixed-use development on Upper College Road.
The CIP also recommends a 2026 General Obligation (GO) Bond project for an Integrated Health Building.
The Integrated Health Buildin g would provide expanded programming to support interprofessional education and clinical training in the health disciplines.
URI is currently contemplating the construction of a new Student Success building on the current site of the Carlotti Building on the quad for the 2028 GO Bond.

Slides 8, 9, and 11 of the enclosed presentation highlight in blue changes from the Draft CIP reviewed by the committee in April, as follows: • We are repeating our full ask for Campus Accessibility and Building Envelope impr ovements, both of which will likely be funded in part by the legislature this year. • The former Blue Technology Innovation Center is now named the Ocean Technology Innovation Center, which was recently awarded funding by the Department of Commerce. • The project costs for Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 2 have been increased slightly to include additional donations to support equipment, and the project cost for repairing the bulkhead at Allen Harbor has been increased after an initial design effort. Recommendation: I recommend that the Board of Trustees approve the enclosed University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2027-FY2031. Supporting Information: Please see University of Rhode Island FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan Enclosure Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2027-FY2031 as presented.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN FY27-FY31 Presentation to Board of Trustees – Finance and Facilities June 26, 2025

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically in July. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? • There are 5 levels of approval. They are: • University of Rhode Island - Facilities Committee (internal) (March & May) • University of Rhode Island - President’s Executive Council (March & May) • University of Rhode Island - Board of Trustees (April & June) • Executive Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July-December) • Final Recommended Capital Budget by the Governor’s Office (Third week of January) • Legislative Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) • Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 28% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.

DATE: February 3, 2025 SUBJECT: Discussion Item: Review of Information to Bondholders FY 2024 Purpose of Submittal: To provide an overview of the required information sent to Bondholders upon issuance of new bonds. Points to Consider: The University is required to have an Official Statement for each bond offering that is issued through Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation. As part of the official statement, the University is required to provide information relating to the University of Rhode Island in Appendix A of the Official Statement. Some key areas included in Appendix A are governance, senior leadership, research, academic program, student demographics, financial aid, facilities, and financial information. Management updates this information on an annual basis in anticipation of future borrowings. Appendix A also serves a useful reference document for Board of Trustees members. A-2 APPENDIX A INFORMATION RELATING TO THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND XX, xx, 2025 Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation 33 Broad Street, Suite 200 Providence, Rhode Island 02903 Dear Members of the Corporation: The University of Rhode Island (the “University” or “URI”) is pleased to submit the following information.
This letter and the information contained herein are submitted to the Rhode Island Health and Educational Building Corporation (“RIHEBC”) for inclusion in its Official Statement relating to its Higher Education Facility Revenue Bonds, University of Rhode Island Educational and General Revenue Issue, Series 20xx (The Series 20xx Bonds).
OVERVIEW OF THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND The University had its beginning as the State Agricultural School chartered in 1888.
The federal Morrill Act of 1862 provided the framework within which the school became the land-grant institution of the State of Rhode Island (the “State”) and in 1892, the school became the Rhode Island College of Agricultural and Mechanic Arts.
The first class of 17 members was graduated two years l ater.

In 1909 the name of the College was changed to Rhode Island State College and the program of study was revised and expanded.
In 1951, the college became known as the University of Rhode Island by act of the State’s General Assembly.
The University of Rhode Island is the S tate’s flagship land and sea grant research institution, with a commitment to urban initiatives.
A student-centered research institution, URI actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to advance knowledge and t o develop informed residents and leaders.
URI is committed to high -quality education, community engagement, and solving the world’s most important challenges.
Situated on the traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the Niantic People, URI strives to create a diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers, learners, and community members.
URI’s Strategic Plan, Focus URI 2023-2033, lays out the strategic vision for the University for the next decade, outlining four strategic priorities and the actions the University will take to achieve them:

A-3 Strategic Priority 1: Broaden the University’s impact through a reinvigorated commitment to its land- and sea-grant missions and the State of Rhode Island Strategic Priority 2: Enhance student achievement by cultivating an engaged and inclusive learning environment Strategic Priority 3: Foster an inclusive, people-centered culture Strategic Priority 4: Implement leading-edge administrative and financial systems and practices to power the University of the future The University’s main campus in Kingston, RI encompasses approximately 1,400 acres in Kingston, 30 miles south of Providence in the nor theastern metropolitan corridor between New York and Boston.
The 165-acre Narragansett Bay Campus (the “Bay Campus”), located six miles to the east overlooking the west passage of the Narragansett Bay, is home to the Graduate School of Oceanography , and the Ocean Engineering Department of the College of Engineering, and the College of Environment and Life Sciences.
In Providence, the University offers degree programs and non- credit courses and workshops in various locations.

In the western section of the State, 20 miles from Kingston, the 2,300 acres of woods, fields, streams and ponds on the W.
Alton Jones Campus are the site of research by various principal investigators.
The University offers degree programs through the doctoral level.
The University had a combined graduate, undergraduate and dual high school enrollment headcount of 14,452 students for the fall 2023 official reporting.
First year applications for fall 2023 were once again at record levels with 25,391 applications.
GOVERNANCE The Board of Governors for Higher Education became the governing body for the University in 1981, until the Board of Education assumed governance in January 2013.
In 2014, the Board of Education created two councils, including the Council on Postsecondary Education (the “Council”) which exercised oversight of the University, Rhode Island College (“RIC”), and the Community College of Rhode Island (“CCRI”).
On February 1, 2020, governance of the University was transferred to the newly constituted Board of Trustees for the University of Rhode Island (the “Board of Trustees” or the “URI Board”), whose purpose is the oversight of the University .

The Board of Education and the Council will continue to provide oversight for RIC and CCRI .
The URI Board assumed all the powers and duties with respect to the University formerly assigned to the Board of Education and the Council.
The State continues to oversee State funding of higher education, approve borrowing and drive education policy.
The University is held to meeting performance measures required by the State .
The new organizational structure for URI did not materially change the funding or financing arrangements of the State's three public higher education institutions, except in that the URI Board of Trustees has final approval of tuition and mandatory fee rates.
The new URI Board continues to share responsibility for its portion of previously issued bonds for the State’s colleges, which include debt issued by all three public higher institutions in the State: URI, Rhode Island College, and the Community College of Rhode Island.
The enabling legislation creating the Board of Trustees is codified in Rhode Island General Laws Title 16, Chapter 32.

A-4 The Trustees were originally appointed with staggered terms to ensure continuity on the Board.
On an annual basis, trustees are considered for appointment and reappointment by the Governor and are confirmed by the State legislature by the end of each legislative session, typically by June.
Three-year terms will again be staggered, as shown by the term expiration dates of those Trustees who have been reappointed to date.
The Faculty Senate was authorized in 1960 by the general faculty to conduct any business assigned to the faculty by law or by the Rhode Island Board of Educ ation/Council on Postsecondary Education and now by the Board of Trustees.
